content.punchline: A hybrid three-strategy framework turns six targets into concrete per-patient cocktail drafts for 61% of a real cohort

slides.speaker_notes_seed: S2 closed on six replicated targets. The immediate audience question is: can phage actually hit them? This section answers in three moves — build the phage-evidence stack, expose the structural gap that makes a pure cocktail impossible, then show what the hybrid framework delivers for real patients. The honest close: this is a design template, not a ready-to-deploy cocktail. The E1 targets are replicated; the framework is concrete; multi-center validation is the next required step.

step_caption: Layer 1 — Literature curation (NB12) classifies all six Tier-A targets into four categories: clinical-trial-stage, lytic-literature, temperate-only, or coverage-GAP
Layer 2 — PhageFoundry experimental matrix (NB13) quantifies per-strain susceptibility for E. coli AIEC across 17,672 tested pairs; greedy set-cover yields the 5-phage cocktail
Layer 3 — HMP2 endogenous phageome (NB14) corroborates E. coli phage carriage in-vivo; confirms coverage gap persists across all three evidence layers for gut-anaerobe targets
content.tool_version_footer: PhageFoundry Gaborieau 2025-10-02 · Kaiju 1.10 · HMP2 viromics NB14

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §'Pillar 4 deliverables' (NB12+NB13+NB14 stack). NB12 is qualitative literature-based stratification — puts each Tier-A species into one of four buckets before any experiment. NB13 is the quantitative layer: 96 phages × 188 E. coli strains, 17,672 susceptibility pairs, 22% susceptibility rate — this is the definitive cocktail-design dataset. NB14 adds endogenous in-vivo corroboration: Podoviridae +0.18 and Myoviridae +0.13 Spearman correlations with E. coli confirm phage presence at the gut level. The key output is not just the cocktail — it is the 2-tier stratification (phage-feasible vs. phage-GAP) that will drive the hybrid framework on the next slide.

content.subtitle: E. coli AIEC strain coverage from a 5-phage cocktail
content.sub_pointer: DIJ07_P2 + LF73_P1 + AL505_Ev3 + 55989_P2 + LF110_P2 — comparable to the EcoActive 7-phage clinical-trial cocktail
content.source_footer: REPORT.md §NB13; greedy set-cover on 96 phages × 188 PhageFoundry-tested strains

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §NB13 (line: '5-phage cocktail covering 94.7 % of 188 strains'). The headline number is directly from NB13's greedy minimum-set-cover result. The EcoActive comparison is also in REPORT: 'comparable in size to the EcoActive 7-phage clinical-trial cocktail.' One caveat to surface in notes: the 94.7% coverage is on PhageFoundry-tested E. coli strains, not UC Davis patient isolates — applicability to specific patients requires an AIEC strain-resolution diagnostic (flagged as near-term in NB17 roadmap). E. coli itself is present in only 35% of UC Davis patients — so the cocktail is directly applicable to ~8/23 patients. This caveat connects forward to the hybrid framework slide.

content.title: Phage-feasible vs. phage-gap targets force a hybrid 3-strategy framework
left_col_content: E. coli AIEC — Tier-1: 5-phage cocktail at 94.7% strain coverage; EcoActive clinical-trial precedent
E. lenta — lytic phage PMBT5 from literature; Tier-2
E. bolteae — lytic phage PMBT24 from literature; Tier-2 with BA-axis monitoring
right_col_content: H. hathewayi (NB05 score 4.0) — coverage-GAP across all 3 phage layers; alternative: GAG-degrading enzyme inhibitors
F. plautii (NB05 score 3.3) — coverage-GAP; dominant E1 design constraint (78% of patients); alternative: BA-binding co-therapy
M. gnavus (NB05 score 3.8) — temperate-only (6 phages, none lytic); alternative: lytic-locked engineering or glucorhamnan biochemical target

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §'Pillar 4 closure synthesis' (NB12 4-class stratification) and §'Pillar 5 Principle 1'. Key framing: the 2 phage-GAP species (H. hathewayi score 4.0, F. plautii score 3.3) are the HIGHEST-scored Tier-A targets — the gap falls precisely on the most important targets. M. gnavus is temperate-only, not a complete gap, but no lytic phage is available. This slide earns the 'hybrid 3-strategy' label: (1) direct phage targeting, (2) alternative therapies for GAP species, (3) limited/engineered for M. gnavus. This is the honest pivot — pure phage cocktail is NOT feasible for any E1 patient. The speaker should name this explicitly before moving to patient drafts.

content.title: The hybrid framework delivers concrete cocktail drafts for 14 of 23 UC Davis patients (61%)
bullets: All 9 E1 patients receive concrete cocktails (PMBT24 + PMBT5 + AIEC 5-phage if E. coli present); mean 4.89 targets per patient
4 of 6 E3 patients receive concrete drafts; E0 patients (n=7) lack drafts because their priority targets (H. hathewayi, M. gnavus) fall in phage GAP

F. plautii — present in 78% of patients including all 9 E1 — is deprioritized as cocktail component and co-administered as BA-binding co-therapy (highest BA-coupling cost + Pillar-4 GAP = double penalty)

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §'Finding 15' (NB15 + NB17 master table; line: '14 of 23 patients (61%) have concrete phage cocktail drafts'). All three bullets grounded in NB15 per-patient profile table. The 78% F. plautii carriage is from the same table ('Per-target prescribing rate: F. plautii 78%'). The 4-category patient stratification: A (Active+many-targets, mostly E1), B (Active+few-targets), C (Quiescent), D (Mixed/longitudinal). Important scoping: the 61% figure is the deliverable of this analysis — it is not a generalizability claim. The framework is a design template; multi-center cohort validation is the explicitly flagged next step (NB17 roadmap). This slide closes the 'per-patient drafts' promise from the throughline.

content.title: Patient 6967's E1→E3 drift is consistent with five state-dependent dosing rules

bullets.claim: M. gnavus 14× expansion marks ecotype drift and is consistent with qPCR as a cheap clinical proxy — preliminary evidence that a 5-fold change could trigger ecotype re-test without full metagenomics (n=1; hypothesis, not validated assay)
bullets.evidence_pointer: REPORT.md §'Finding 16' (NB16): M. gnavus 0.53 → 7.45 reads; cocktail Jaccard visit 1 × visit 2 = 0.60

bullets.claim: Universal Tier-1 trio (M. gnavus + H. hathewayi + E. lenta) spans both ecotypes and is a robust cocktail backbone; F. plautii is E1-specific (drop on E1→E3 transition) and E. coli is E3-specific
bullets.evidence_pointer: REPORT.md §'Pillar 5 closure synthesis' Principle 4; Novel Contribution #24 (NB16 §5)

bullets.claim: Ecotype is dynamic, not static: design templates must be state-dependent, with re-test every 3-6 months for active-disease CD patients on phage therapy — multi-cohort longitudinal validation required before clinical deployment
bullets.evidence_pointer: REPORT.md §'Pillar 5 Principle 4' (NB16); Limitations: 'n=1 longitudinal trajectory; qPCR proxy is a hypothesis, not validated assay'

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §'Finding 16' and §'Novel Contribution #24' (NB16 longitudinal). This is the deck's honest close. The A12 analysis is ⚠ partial: n=1 patient (6967), and the ecotype call confidence at visit 2 is only 0.41 (moderate). The M. gnavus 14× expansion is a real quantitative observation, but the clinical threshold (5-fold qPCR trigger) is a hypothesis derived from one data point. Slide title and bullet 1 use 'consistent with' and 'preliminary evidence' explicitly — mandatory for partial-strength analyses. The 5 dosing rules (from Novel Contribution #24) are the deliverable but should be framed as design principles, not validated clinical protocols. The deck closes here: the framework is concrete, per-patient, and honest about what needs prospective multi-cohort validation before clinical use.
